findings.title: `enableSqlExpressions` always returns false and ignores the feature flag it reads
findings.description:
Both branches return `false`, so the `IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` lookup has no effect. The local `enabled` is assigned the negation of the flag, so it actually means "disabled", which makes the function read as if it honours the toggle.

Consequences:
- The `sqlExpressions` toggle is now a no-op for this path, though it is still registered in `pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go:1083` as "Enables using SQL and DuckDB functions as Expressions."
- The rest of the `QueryTypeSQL` case in `pkg/expr/reader.go:133-138` is unreachable.

If SQL expressions are meant to be unconditionally off while the backend is a stub, say so directly: return the error in the case and drop the helper, or reduce it to `return false` with a comment. If the flag is meant to gate it, the function should be `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`.

Minor style points: the helper takes the receiver as a parameter rather than being a method, and Go initialism convention would be `enableSQLExpressions`.

findings.title: Legacy parse path is not gated and reports "not implemented" as an invalid-SQL 400
findings.description:
The new gate only covers `ReadQuery`, which `buildCMDNode` reaches only when `FlagExpressionParser` is on (`pkg/expr/nodes.go:123`). With that flag off, `TypeSQL` still goes through `UnmarshalSQLCommand` → `NewSQLCommand` → `sql.TablesList`.

`TablesList` now always fails, because the stub `RunCommands` returns `errors.New("not implemented")` (`pkg/expr/sql/db.go:16-18`). `NewSQLCommand` then maps that failure to `errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql", "error reading SQL command")` and logs "invalid sql query" at Warn (`pkg/expr/sql_command.go:30-35`).

So the same disabled feature produces two different errors:
- **Parser path:** a plain `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`.
- **Legacy path:** a 400 that blames the user's SQL, plus a log line per request that misdescribes the cause.

Gate once, at a point both paths share (for example in `NewSQLCommand`), with a single typed error. A package-level sentinel in `pkg/expr/sql` in place of the three duplicated `errors.New("not implemented")` strings would let callers distinguish it via `errors.Is`.

findings.title: No tests cover the new gating or stub behaviour
findings.description:
The change adds a new error path in `ReadQuery` and a new `DB` type, with no tests for either.
- `pkg/expr/reader_test.go` has no SQL case.
- Every test in `pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go` starts with `t.Skip()`.
- `TestNewCommand` in `pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go:9` is also skipped, and its fallback matches the string "feature is not enabled", which nothing in the code emits.

A table case in `reader_test.go` asserting that a `type: "sql"` query returns the not-implemented error, with the flag both on and off, would pin the intended behaviour. It would also have exposed the always-false gate above.

findings.title: Stub `DB` has an unused method, no doc comments, and DuckDB-specific code left around it
findings.description:
- `(*DB).TablesList` at `pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12-14` has no callers; every call site uses the package-level `sql.TablesList` in `parser.go`. It is dead on arrival and duplicates that function's name.
- The exported `DB`, its methods and `NewInMemoryDB` have no doc comments, so nothing says this is a deliberate placeholder for the removed engine.
- `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23-26` still names the variable `duckDB` and builds a DuckDB-only `SELECT json_serialize_sql('…')` command for a backend that cannot run it.
- `SQLCommand.Execute` (`pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-105`) still builds frames and calls `QueryFramesInto`, which can only fail.

Either trim the stub to what is called and document it as a placeholder, or put a small interface in front of it so a real implementation can be swapped in.

findings.title: Stale `go-duck` checksum remains in `go.work.sum`
findings.description: `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck v0.3.1` entries are still in `go.work.sum`, although no `go.mod` or Go source in the tree references the module. They are harmless and outside this diff, but could be dropped for a complete removal.

findings.title: Dependency removal is consistent with the source changes
findings.description: The `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck` requirement and the indirect-only entries (`apache/thrift`, `JohnCGriffin/overflow`, `klauspost/asmfmt`, `minio/asm2plan9s`, `minio/c2goasm`, `hairyhenderson/go-which`, `iancoleman/orderedmap`) are removed from `go.mod`, with matching `go.sum` edits. `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` and `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` no longer import the `duck` package. The stub signatures in `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` match their call sites (`RunCommands([]string) (string, error)` and `QueryFramesInto(string, string, []*data.Frame, *data.Frame) error`).

structured_findings.summary: `enableSqlExpressions` always returns false and ignores the feature flag it reads
Legacy parse path is not gated and reports "not implemented" as an invalid-SQL 400
No tests cover the new gating or stub behaviour
Stub `DB` has an unused method, no doc comments, and DuckDB-specific code left around it
Dependency removal is consistent with the source changes
